subject: tu:game/world/items
value: Item (b) of claim.gamemode-raw-site-inventory.20260831.v1 -- items.c declaring `extern u32 gGameMode` where every other TU uses `s32` -- is CONFIRMED as a real cross-TU declaration divergence and is now FIXED and byte-gated. s32 is the correct spelling: the PDB type is `enum e_mode` (int-ranked), 15 of the 16 consumer TUs already declare s32, and items.c's own code betrayed the mismatch by casting the value back with `(s32)gGameMode` at three sites in order to compare it. Changing the declaration to s32 and dropping all three now-redundant casts is BYTE-IDENTICAL (defake_gate check --rebuild = GATE OK against a 52-function / 41-at-real-0 baseline), so the divergence was cosmetic in codegen terms but was actively generating fakematch casts -- a defake win with no matching risk. Verified further by a full green ninja with build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK and project progress unmoved at 98.05% fuzzy / 60.99% matched. ONE u32-flavoured use was deliberately KEPT unchanged: `gGameMode & 0x8000` at items.c:1255 is the MA_/MG_ group-bit classification idiom documented in include/game/gamemode.h, not a mode comparison, so it needs no enum constant and no cast either way. TOOLING GAP worth closing: tools/gdl/externcheck.py did not flag this, because it reports only float/int-class conflicts and u32-vs-s32 share a storage class; the same blind spot hides the pointer-vs-int divergence on lbl_80344290 recorded in claim.sndfxinit-first-param-is-a-mode-not-a-pointer.20260831.v1. Extending externcheck to same-size signedness and pointer-vs-integer divergence would surface both classes automatically instead of relying on a per-wave manual sweep.
